image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) floating on dark, rippling water. The duck features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a brown speckled chest, and greyish-brown body feathers. Its tail is curled upward, displaying black and white feathers. The bill appears yellow-green with a dark tip. The reflection of the duck is visible in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad and flat, with a yellow-green base transitioning to a darker tip, matching the description.
The eye is visible as a small dark spot on the side of the green head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a floating duck, appearing compact and buoyant. The plumage texture looks dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, white neck ring, and brown/grey body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are submerged underwater and completely occluded by the body and water surface; they cannot be visually verified.
The folded wings are visible along the side of the body, showing the characteristic speculum (blue/white patch) and structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is clearly visible at the rear, featuring the characteristic upward curl of the central black feathers typical of male mallards.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The iridescent green head has a slightly overly smooth, plastic-like sheen compared to natural feather micro-texture, though this may be due to lighting/wetness.
The very tip of the bill seems to blend slightly into the water line without a sharp meniscus break, suggesting minor geometric ambiguity.
The reflection is somewhat generic and lacks the precise distortion expected from the specific ripples around the body, appearing slightly 'painted on'.
